paper.title: Ability or Finances as Constraints on Entrepreneurship? Evidence from Survival Rates in a Natural Experiment
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement is printed. The paper states that the five data sources are 'made available through Statistics Denmark' (p. …

registers.name_in_paper: the official Danish Civil Registration System (CPR Registeret)
registers.role: linkage and sample frame: identifies all individuals' legal parents and provides a unique identifying number across individuals, households, and time

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish Cause-of-Death Register at the Danish National Board of Health (Sundhedsstyrelsen)
registers.role: treatment: cause of death (ICD-10) used to classify household terminations as sudden and unexpected
variables_mentioned: R95-R97 sudden death by unknown cause
V90-V99, X00-X59, X86-X90 other accidents and violence

registers.name_in_paper: Employment data from Statistics Denmark's IDA database
registers.role: treatment and outcomes: identifies whether individuals become, and survive as, entrepreneurs (self-employed), and whether their parents were entrepreneurs
variables_mentioned: employment status (filings from firms and public agencies in the last week of November)
self-employment (50% of total income from entrepreneurial profit)

registers.name_in_paper: Income and wealth information from the official records at the Danish Tax and Customs Administration (SKAT)
registers.role: treatment (inherited wealth, net wealth), outcomes (entrepreneurial profit, retained earnings, total income) and controls (pre-entrepreneurship income and wealth)
variables_mentioned: total income (labor income + financial income + entrepreneurial profit)

registers.name_in_paper: Education records from the Danish Ministry of Education
registers.role: controls and matching characteristic: years of completed schooling
variables_mentioned: completed (formal and informal) courses of education

linkages: Beneficiaries (offspring) linked to their suddenly deceased legal parents through the Civil Registration System (CPR Registeret) identifiers
Deceased parents linked to their ICD-10 cause of death from the Cause-of-Death Register, to select sudden deaths
Individuals linked by CPR number over time to IDA employment status, SKAT income and wealth records, and education records

Treated beneficiaries linked one-to-many (entry analysis) or one-to-one (performance analysis) to exactly matched control individuals on age, gender, length of education, income vigintile, wealth vigintile and year
Column 4 of Table 3 additionally matches on parental wealth; column 3 of Table 7 matches on parental wealth instead of individual wealth

sample.universe: The population of adult Danes in the period between 1995 and 2007
sample.unit_of_observation: Individual (beneficiary; entrepreneur), and entrepreneur-year for the pooled performance regressions of Tables 6 and 7
selection_rules: 83,602 terminations of households between 1995 and 2001 (last living parent dies, or both parents die within the same calendar year), restricted to cases in which all beneficiaries are offspring
Of these, 12,068 terminations classified as sudden death(s) from the ICD-10 cause of death (12.5% of natural deaths qualify)
Linking the deceased to their beneficiaries (1.60 beneficiaries per terminated household) gives 19,329 individuals who experience a wealth windfall
Focus on individuals who inherit in 1995-2001 and start a business in the following year, leaving a five-year evaluation period
Split into 1,123 preshock entrepreneurs (5.8%) and 18,206 preinheritance nonentrepreneurs; the analysis of entry uses the nonentrepreneurs
Exact one-to-many matching on age, gender, education level, preinheritance income vigintile and wealth vigintile in the same year reduces the entry sample to 18,009 beneficiaries

377 (2.1%) of the matched beneficiaries become self-employed; 22 beneficiaries who inherit from an entrepreneurial estate and subsequently become entrepreneurs are excluded, leaving 355 potentially constrained entrepreneurs

Exact one-to-one matching of constrained entrepreneurs to unconstrained entrepreneurs who start a business at the same time (same age, gender, education, pre-entrepreneurship income and wealth vigintiles) fails for 51 individuals, leaving 304 matched pairs
Pooling the five-year window after business formation gives 3,023 entrepreneur-year observations (3,013 for the income regressions)
Table 7 column 4 matches 140 constrained entrepreneurs to unconstrained entrepreneurs who inherit in years 1 to 3 after business formation, relaxing exact matching on age
sample.period: Population data 1995-2007; inheritance events (sudden household terminations) 1995-2001; business formation in the following year with a five-year evaluation period
sample.n_observations: 19,329 beneficiaries; 18,009 matched beneficiaries in the entry regressions; 3,023 pooled entrepreneur-year observations in the main performance regression (1,898 for the competing-risk model)
sample.n_individuals: 19,329 beneficiaries of 12,068 sudden household terminations; 18,206 preinheritance nonentrepreneurs; 355 potentially constrained entrepreneurs, of whom 304 matched to unconstrained entrepreneurs

construction_notes: All income and wealth amounts are indexed to constant 2000 Danish kroner (DKK); one Euro is equivalent to DKK 7.45
Inherited wealth is measured in million year-2000 DKK; inherited wealth squared is its square

Self-employment: Statistics Denmark classifies individuals as self-employed whenever 50% of their total income originates from entrepreneurial profit; individuals so classified obtain on average more than 90% of total income from entrepreneurship

Total income = labor income + financial income + entrepreneurial profit (SKAT definition); entrepreneurial profit is pretax profit from self-employment including potential gains from selling the business
Net wealth (SKAT) covers bank deposits, bank loans, property values, mortgages, stocks, mutual funds and bonds; it excludes cash outside bank accounts, cars, private debt and informal holdings

Estates: children inherit in equal proportional shares under the Danish Inheritance Law of 1964 (at least 50% of the estate); the net worth of the estate is subject to a 15% estate tax above DKK 191,000 (EUR 25,638) in 1998, inflated by a price index thereafter; transfer must be finalized within twelve months of the death
Sudden deaths comprise ICD-10 codes I22-I23, I46, I50, I60-I69, R95-R97 (natural) and V00-V89, V90-V99, X00-X59, X86-X90 (unnatural, excluding suicide and violence by relatives of the decedent)

Matching uses vigintiles (twenty groups of equal frequency) of the preinheritance income and wealth distributions; in case of several matches in the performance analysis, the match with the closest pre-entrepreneurship income is used

Business exits are characterized as success if the entrepreneurial profit reported in the year of exit exceeds DKK 100,000 and as failure otherwise; 16.5% of all exits (54 of 328) are classified as successes
Figure 2 indexes total income to the pre-entrepreneurship and preinheritance level (year -1 = 100)
Figure 1 bins constrained entrepreneurs using the quintile cutoff points of the year-1 entrepreneurial profit distribution of unconstrained entrepreneurs

claims.statement: Among Danish beneficiaries of sudden-death estates who were not previously self-employed, inherited wealth is associated with a positive change in the difference-in-differences of the propensity to become an entrepreneur relative to an exactly matched control group (Table 3, column 1).

register_source.value: Income and wealth records from the official files of the Danish Tax and Customs Administration (SKAT), made available through Statistics Denmark; the paper names no register variable code

definition.value: Windfall wealth received as unexpected inheritance following the sudden death of the last living parent (or of both parents within the same calendar year), measured in million year-2000 DKK; estates are divided equally among the offspring under the Danish Inheritance Law of 1964

timing.value: Inheritance received in the year of the parental sudden death, 1995-2001 (transfer must be finalized within twelve months of the death)

outcome.label: Difference-in-differences of the propensity to become entrepreneur

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark IDA employment database (employment status from firm and public-agency filings in the last week of November each year); Statistics Denmark classifies individuals as self-employed whenever 50% of their total income originates from entrepreneurial profit

definition.value: The difference between an indicator variable for entry of the treated individual into self-employment and the average entry rate of the exactly matched control sample (one-to-many exact match on age, gender, length of education, preinheritance income vigintile and wealth vigintile in the same year)

timing.value: Entry into self-employment in the year following the windfall inheritance (inheritance 1995-2001, entry in the following year)

units.value: probability units (difference-in-differences of entry) per million year-2000 DKK of inherited wealth; marginal effect at the sample means

magnitude.interpretation: Windfall wealth of one million DKK (EUR 134,200) increases the probability of an individual starting her own business by 0.95 percentage points.

estimand.target_population: Treated beneficiaries of sudden-death estates 1995-2001 who were nonentrepreneurs before the windfall
estimand.time_horizon: Entry into self-employment in the year following the windfall inheritance
estimand.formal_query: E[entry | do(inherited wealth = w + 1 million DKK)] - E[entry | do(inherited wealth = w)] for treated beneficiaries, differenced against the matched control group's entry rate, evaluated at the sample means

population.description: Danish beneficiaries of sudden-death estates 1995-2001 who were not self-employed before the parental death (18,206 preinheritance nonentrepreneurs, of whom 18,009 could be exactly matched), together with an exactly matched control group of individuals who did not receive windfall wealth
population.ages: Adults; mean age 41.1 years among preinheritance nonentrepreneur beneficiaries in the year before the death
population.period: Inheritances 1995-2001; population data 1995-2007
population.selection: Beneficiaries (offspring) of households terminated by sudden death, restricted to individuals who were nonentrepreneurs before the windfall and for whom an exact match on age, gender, length of education, preinheritance income vigintile and wealth vigintile in the same year could be found

identification.source_of_variation: Windfall wealth from unexpected inheritance due to the sudden death of the last living parent (or of both parents within the same calendar year) in Denmark, 1995-2001; 12,068 sudden household terminations with 19,329 beneficiaries identified from ICD-10 causes of death

key_assumptions.assumption: The parental death event is unexpected and sudden, so the windfall inheritance is unanticipated and cannot have been acted on before the death
key_assumptions.supported_by: Sample restricted to ICD-10 causes classified as sudden (acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, congestive heart failure, stroke, sudden death by unknown cause, traffic accidents, other accidents and violence excluding suicide and violence by relatives); Table 1 tabulates the classification

key_assumptions.assumption: The death event is uncorrelated with omitted variables that affect the outcome, e.g., the decision to become an entrepreneur
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in footnote 2 as a requirement of the identification strategy; no direct test reported

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on the exact match characteristics (age, gender, length of education, preinheritance income vigintile, preinheritance wealth vigintile, year), treated beneficiaries and control individuals would have had the same entry rate absent the windfall
key_assumptions.supported_by: One-to-many exact matching on these characteristics; difference-in-differences differencing of the entry indicator

key_assumptions.assumption: Children inherit the estate in equal proportional shares, so the windfall size is determined by the parental estate and the number of offspring rather than by the beneficiary
key_assumptions.supported_by: Danish Inheritance Law of 1964 guarantees children at least 50% of the estate; only 2% of the empirically relevant individuals have drafted a will

threats_discussed: Inheritance of entrepreneurial estates could drive the relation between windfall wealth and entry (Hurst and Lusardi 2004)
Intergenerational correlation in wealth, education, occupation and savings preferences could mean inherited wealth proxies for family entrepreneurial propensity
The death event must be uncorrelated with omitted variables affecting the decision to become an entrepreneur
robustness_checks: Indicator for entrepreneurial estate added (Table 3, Column 2) and entrepreneurial estates excluded entirely (Table 3, Column 3)
Control group additionally matched on parental wealth (Table 3, Column 4)
Online appendix: alternative matching procedures (Abadie and Imbens 2006; Hirano and Imbens 2004), omitting control variables, region-year fixed effects, industry-year fixed effects
unresolved_confounders: Intergenerational transmission of entrepreneurial propensity is addressed by matching on parental wealth in column 4 but is not otherwise resolved

estimator.value: OLS cross-sectional regression of the differenced entry indicator; reported coefficients are marginal effects at the sample means

estimation.specification: Cross-sectional regression of the difference between the treated individual's entry indicator and the matched control group's average entry rate on inherited wealth, inherited wealth squared, controls and year fixed effects (no equation printed)
controls: Indicator variables for changes in marital status and family size (marries, divorces, or has children)

source_table.value: Table 3, column 1

adjustment_set.label: Indicators for changes in marital status and family size

ambiguities: The baseline mean is the matched control group's entry rate of 0.83% converted to a proportion (0.0083); the paper prints it as a percentage.

evidence.how: The matched control group's entry rate of 0.83% is expressed as a proportion (0.0083) to match the units of the dependent variable, which is a difference of entry indicators.
Significance read from the star legend in the note to Table 3 ('***, **, and * denote significance at the 1%, 5%, and 10% levels'); the p-value is recorded as less than that level.
